comment: World truth of the goblin investigation on Cinderwatch Pass (docs/design/RESEARCH_STATISTICS_RPG.md §7). Never shown to the player outside a debrief. The distributions are placeholders: keep each habitat's probabilities summing to 1; damage dice come from GLAIVE's weapon table.

kingdom.comment: Placeholders (design §10, D7, D8). Citizens use GLAIVE's PC formulas with +0 bonuses (HP 10, AC 10 + armour); prices are GLAIVE's armour prices.

variation.comment: Every foe outside the study (not a boss) varies per run: offsets drawn from these [value, probability] pairs and added to its stat block's attack bonus and HP. A family can have its own entry under families.

missions.title: 1. Define the threat
missions.brief: Royal Steward: "Goblins raid the farms of the Pass, on the road and at the mire edge. How often does a goblin's attack get through light armour? Before you fight, tell me what we are studying."

options.text: Every goblin that raids the Pass: on the road and in the mire.
options.feedback: Yes. That is the population: the whole group the kingdom asks about.

options.text: The goblins I happen to fight.
options.feedback: Those are your sample. The kingdom asks about every raiding goblin, met or not.

options.text: The goblins near the Waystone Camp.
options.feedback: That is only one place. The farms are all over the Pass.

options.text: One goblin: its first normal attack.
options.feedback: Yes. One goblin, one attack. Three attacks by one goblin are still one goblin.

options.text: Every attack, from any goblin.
options.feedback: A strong goblin that attacks five times would count five times. We count goblins, not swings.

options.text: One fight.
options.feedback: A fight holds several goblins. We want each goblin.

tasks.question: What do we measure about it?

options.text: Whether its strike beats light armour (AC 12): yes or no.
options.feedback: Yes. A yes/no (categorical) variable. The log shows each strike total, so you can tell.

options.text: How many hit points it has.
options.feedback: You never see that number. Measure what you can observe.

options.text: The damage of each miss.
options.feedback: A miss does no damage at all. Damage exists only for hits.

missions.title: 2. Two places, two samples
missions.brief: Start on the road near the camp: those goblins are easy to find. Then visit the Hollow Mire to the north-east. Compare what you see.

tasks.question: What share of your ROAD goblins' first attacks beat light armour (AC 12)? Answer as a decimal, e.g. 0.45.
tasks.hint: Count the road goblins whose eligible strike was 12 or more (or a natural 20). Divide by all road goblins with an eligible attack.

tasks.question: Your mire goblins differ from your road goblins. Why?

options.text: The mire goblins may be a different group. Small samples also vary by chance.
options.feedback: Yes. A difference can come from different groups, from chance, or both. More mire data will tell.

options.text: The road sample was a mistake.
options.feedback: No: it describes the road goblins well. It just says nothing about the mire.

options.text: My armour changed the goblins.
options.feedback: Armour does not change how a goblin strikes. The strike total is the same whatever you wear.

tasks.question: Would 100 more road fights fix an estimate for the whole Pass?

options.text: No. More road data still leaves out the mire.
options.feedback: Right. A bigger sample cuts chance error, not the bias of leaving a group out.

options.text: Yes. A bigger sample is always better.
options.feedback: A bigger sample from the same place repeats the same gap. The mire goblins are still missing.

missions.title: 3. Describe the threat
missions.brief: A citizen has 10 HP. Look at the damage of the hits you have taken. Your first ten hits: {firstDamage}.

tasks.question: What is the mean of your first ten hits' damage?
tasks.hint: Add the ten values and divide by 10.

tasks.question: Is the mean damage enough to judge the danger to a citizen?

options.text: No. The biggest hits matter: one hit of 10 or more drops a citizen.
options.feedback: Yes. The shape of the distribution matters, not just its centre. Look at the right tail.

options.text: Yes. The mean says it all.
options.feedback: Two threats with the same mean can be very different. One of them may drop a citizen in one blow.

missions.title: 4. How sure are we?
missions.brief: With 30 or more goblins, the ledger can show a 95% confidence interval for the share that beats light armour: {interval}.

options.text: If we sampled this way many times, about 95% of intervals made like this would contain the true share.
options.feedback: Yes. The 95% describes the method, over many samples.

options.text: 95% of goblin attacks fall inside this range.
options.feedback: No. The interval is about the share (a proportion), not about single attacks.

options.text: The true share is certainly inside this range.
options.feedback: Not certainly. Some intervals made this way miss. And it only covers the places you sampled.

tasks.question: You want a narrower, fairer interval. Where should you gather more?

options.text: Where my sample is thin compared with the Pass. Not just more of the same road.
options.feedback: Yes. More data narrows the interval; data from the right places makes it fair.

options.text: Anywhere. More is more.
options.feedback: More from one place narrows the interval around the wrong value if that place is not typical.

missions.title: 5. Advise the kingdom
missions.brief: The Steward has 2000 silver. Light armour costs 25, medium 75, for each of 40 citizens (16 on the road, 24 at the mire). Each citizen faces raids; an injury costs the kingdom 100 silver, a death 2000. Money taken below the 500 reserve leaves other needs unpaid. Give your estimate, your interval, and, separately, your purchase.
